note: Prepared from the unit title and the trade's usual practice. An instructor must read and correct it, and mark it Ready, before it is opened for an intake.

unit.title: Diagnose and repair faults in electrical and electronic systems

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A restaurant in Negril reports that its kitchen extractor fan stops after running for about 20 minutes. What should you do before opening anything?
options: Replace the fan motor, since that is the usual cause of this
Ask the staff what happens, when it started and what changed
Fit a larger breaker so that the circuit stops switching off
Bridge out the overload so that the fan keeps running all day

questions.stem: Why is the half-split method useful when tracing a fault along a long control circuit?
options: Each test halves the part of the circuit left to check
It lets you test the circuit with the supply switched on
It means you only ever test the two ends of the circuit
It removes any need to read the drawing before testing

questions.stem: You have seen the symptom and must now open a motor starter to test it. Which order is correct?
options: Prove dead, switch off, lock off and tag, then check the tester
Switch off, prove dead, then lock off only if the job is long
Switch off, lock off, tag, check tester, prove dead, check tester
Lock off, check the tester, switch off, tag, then prove dead

questions.stem: A breaker trips the instant it is reset, even with every load unplugged. Which fault is most likely?
options: An overload from too many appliances on the circuit
A loose connection at one of the socket outlets
A lamp that has burnt out in one of the light fittings
A short circuit or earth fault in the fixed wiring

questions.stem: A breaker trips after a water pump has run for about half an hour, but never when it starts. What does this point to?
options: A short circuit between line and neutral in the cable
A dead short to earth inside the pump's terminal box
An overload, such as a pump bearing that is failing
A wrong colour code used on the pump's supply cable

questions.stem: An RCD on a house supply trips at random, most often after heavy rain. What is a likely cause?
options: The circuit carries more current than its breaker's rating
The supply voltage from the power company is a little low
The RCD's test button has been pressed too many times
Water in an outdoor fitting causing leakage to earth

questions.stem: When hunting for an earth fault with an insulation resistance tester, why must electronic devices be disconnected first?
options: They make the tester read higher than the true value
The test voltage can damage them or give false readings
They run on direct current, so the tester cannot measure them
The tester's battery will go flat if they stay connected

questions.stem: A final circuit has a very low insulation reading from line to earth. You split it in the middle: the first half now reads high and the second half reads low. Where should you look next?
options: In the second half of the circuit
In the first half of the circuit
At the breaker in the distribution board
In the tester, which must be faulty

questions.stem: Which instrument is used to measure the low resistance of each winding of a small single-phase motor, once it is isolated?
options: A non-contact voltage detector
A clamp meter set to its current range
An insulation tester set to 1000 V
A low-resistance ohmmeter or multimeter

questions.stem: A capacitor-start motor on a compressor hums but will not start. When it is isolated, the shaft turns freely by hand. Which part is most likely faulty?
options: The run winding, which has burnt out completely
The start capacitor or the starting switch
The supply cable, which is too large for the motor
The motor's bearings, which have seized solid

questions.stem: Why must a capacitor be discharged before you test or touch it, even when the supply is isolated?
options: It can hold a dangerous charge after the supply is off
It will lose its value if it is tested while charged
It only holds a charge while the supply is switched on
The meter reads any stored charge as a short circuit

questions.stem: A run capacitor marked 30 µF ±5% reads 22 µF on a capacitance meter. What should you do?
options: Leave it in, because any reading near the mark is fine
Fit a 22 µF capacitor in its place to match the reading
Replace it with one of the same value and voltage rating
Fit one with a lower voltage rating, as it costs less

questions.stem: On the diode test range, a good silicon diode reads about 0.6 V one way round. What should it show the other way round?
options: Open circuit (OL), as no current should flow
About 0.6 V again, the same as the first way
Zero volts, which shows the diode is working
About 1.2 V, which is double the first reading

questions.stem: A DC power supply in an alarm panel works, but its output has far more ripple (AC wobble) than normal. Which part is the most likely cause?
options: The fuse on the transformer's primary side
The on/off switch on the front of the panel
The main smoothing (filter) capacitor
The indicator lamp on the front of the panel

questions.stem: On a 12 V training board powered by the instructor, a 5 V regulator has 12 V at its input and 0 V at its output, and nothing is shorted on the output side. What is most likely?
options: The 12 V input is too low for the regulator to work
The output capacitor is too large in value for it
The board's earth track is carrying too much current
The regulator has failed and needs replacing

questions.stem: Why do you wear an earthed wrist strap when replacing a chip on a control board?
options: To protect yourself from the board's supply voltage
To stop static charge from damaging the parts
To keep hot solder from sticking to your fingers
To earth the board's supply circuit while you work

questions.stem: A 2 A time-delay (slow-blow) fuse has blown in a motor controller. Which replacement is correct?
options: A 2 A quick-blow fuse, as that is all the van stock has
A 2 A time-delay fuse, after the cause has been found
A 5 A time-delay fuse, so that it will not blow again
A short length of wire, until a new fuse is bought

questions.stem: A 24 V AC relay will not pull in. With the circuit dead, its coil reads open circuit on the ohms range. What does this tell you?
options: The coil winding is broken, so the relay must be replaced
The coil is fine, because relay coils always read open
The contacts are welded shut and need to be cleaned
The coil needs a higher voltage to pull in properly

questions.stem: In a direct-on-line starter, the motor starts when START is pressed but stops as soon as the button is let go. Which fault fits this?
options: The overload relay has tripped and needs resetting
The STOP button's contacts are stuck open
The hold-in (auxiliary) contact is not making
The main fuses on the supply side have blown

questions.stem: A motor's overload relay keeps tripping. The motor is drawing more than the full-load current on its nameplate. What should you do?
options: Turn the overload setting up until it stops tripping
Replace the overload relay with a larger one
Bridge out the overload contact while you look further
Check the driven load, the bearings and the supply

questions.stem: A three-phase motor hums and will not start, and one of its three supply fuses has blown. What is this condition called?
options: Phase reversal
Under-loading
Single-phasing
Star connection

questions.stem: A distribution board has a burnt smell, and one breaker terminal shows heat marks. What is the most likely cause?
options: The breaker is rated far too low for the circuit's load
The board was painted with the wrong type of paint
The cable on that breaker is larger than it needs to be
A loose connection, causing high resistance and heat

questions.stem: A light in a hotel corridor flickers off and on whenever a nearby door slams. Which fault is most likely?
options: A burnt-out lamp in the fitting nearest the door
A loose connection in a switch, box or fitting
Low supply voltage at the hotel's main board
Too many lamps fitted on the lighting circuit

questions.stem: Lights dim badly each time a large motor starts on the same long sub-main. What is the most likely cause?
options: Voltage drop from the motor's high starting current
A short circuit inside one of the light fittings
An open circuit in the lighting circuit's switch
A broken protective conductor on the lighting circuit

questions.stem: On a 110/220 V supply to a house, the instructor measures very high voltage at the 110 V outlets on one side and very low voltage on the other. Which fault does this point to?
options: A blown fuse in the water heater's own supply
A breaker that is too large on one of the circuits
Too many outlets connected on one of the circuits
A broken or loose connection in the shared neutral

questions.stem: A metal-cased drill has given its user a slight tingle, and it has been taken out of use. Which test should be done on it first?
options: Polarity at the outlet it was plugged into
Earth continuity from the plug to the metal case
Its speed when drilling into hard concrete
The length of the carbon brushes in the motor

questions.stem: When is it usually better to replace a faulty item than to repair it?
options: When repair costs near a new one, or parts cannot be had
Whenever the client has owned the item for over a year
Whenever the fault takes more than ten minutes to find
When the item is still under the maker's warranty

questions.stem: When replacing a failed contactor, what must the new one match?
options: Only the size of the case, so it fits the same space
The colour and the maker, so it looks like the old one
The coil voltage, current rating and duty for the load
Only the number of terminals, so the old wires reach

questions.stem: You have replaced a through-hole part on a circuit board. Which describes a good solder joint?
options: Smooth, shiny and concave, wetting both pad and lead
A large round ball of solder sitting on top of the pad
A dull grey joint with small cracks around the lead
Solder running across to the next pad for extra strength

questions.stem: After repairing a fault in a pump control panel, what must happen before it is handed back?
options: Close the panel and tell the client it should be fine now
Leave the old faulty part inside the panel as a record
Dead tests, then a function test by a competent person
Switch it on, and leave if the breaker does not trip

questions.stem: The fuse in a pool pump's control has blown for the third time this month. Each time it was replaced and the pump worked. What should you do now?
options: Fit a larger fuse so that the pump can keep running
Replace the fuse again and leave a spare in the panel
Tell the client that fuses are expected to blow often
Find the root cause before fitting another fuse

questions.stem: Why should you write down the readings you take during fault-finding on the job sheet?
options: So the client can be charged for each reading taken
To show the cause, back up the repair and help next time
Because the meter's memory can only hold a few readings
So the sheet looks full when the supervisor checks it

questions.stem: Which drawing is most useful for following how a control circuit works, step by step?
options: The floor plan of the building
The schematic (circuit) diagram
The outside layout drawing of the panel
The drawing of the cable routes

questions.stem: An LED panel light with a separate driver flickers. A panel that is known to be good, fitted in its place, also flickers. What is the most likely fault?
options: The driver, or a loose connection to it
The first panel, which must be replaced
The size of the room the light is fitted in
The colour temperature of the LED panel

questions.stem: A relay coil switched by a transistor keeps destroying the transistor. Which missing part is the most likely cause?
options: A fuse in series with the relay's contacts
A resistor fitted across the relay's contacts
A diode across the relay coil
A larger heat sink fitted on the relay coil

questions.stem: A pump will not start even when its tank is empty. With the circuit isolated, the tank's float switch reads open circuit in both float positions. Where is the fault?
options: In the pump motor's start capacitor
In the controller's main supply fuse
In the pump's non-return valve
In the float switch itself

questions.stem: A competent person may scan a loaded distribution board with a thermal imaging camera. What does this help to find?
options: The age of each cable in the board
Which breakers came from the wrong maker
Hot spots from loose or overloaded parts
Earth faults on switched-off circuits

questions.stem: After a repair, which item belongs on the job report to the client?
options: The technician's opinion of the client's premises
A list of all the other jobs done that same day
The cost of the technician's own hand tools
The fault, its cause, the work done and the tests

questions.stem: A resistor on a board looks burnt. Before ordering a new one, what should you find out?
options: Only its colour, so that the new one looks the same
Its value, its power rating and why it overheated
The age of the board that it was fitted to
Whether the maker or a repairer fitted it

questions.stem: A 220 V water heater trips its RCD. With the circuit isolated, an insulation test shows the element has a low resistance to earth. What should be done?
options: Replace the element and test again before it is switched on
Swap the RCD for a plain breaker so that it stops tripping
Disconnect the protective conductor from the heater's case
Turn the thermostat down so the element runs cooler

questions.stem: A repair needs a factory's main pump shut down. What should the technician agree with the client before starting?
options: Nothing, because a repair comes before all production
Only the price of the parts, as labour is not charged
The colour of the new cable that is going to be used
When the shutdown starts, how long it lasts, who is told

questions.stem: Which lead of a diode is next to the band printed on its body?
options: The anode
The cathode
The power rating
The gate

questions.stem: After a three-phase motor is reconnected, it runs the wrong way. Once it is isolated, what is the correct fix?
options: Swap any two of the three supply phases
Swap the protective conductor and one phase
Reverse the neutral in the motor's terminal box
Move all three phases round by one terminal

questions.stem: A variable speed drive shows a fault code on its display. What is the best first step?
options: Reset it again and again until the code goes away
Replace the drive, since any code means it has failed
Look up the code in the maker's manual
Take off the drive's cover with the power still on

questions.stem: A heating element is marked 220 V, 2200 W. When it is isolated, about what resistance should it read?

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is a soldered connection called that looks dull or cracked and does not make good contact?
A capacitor is marked 30 µF. What fraction of a farad does the prefix micro (µ) mean?
About how many volts are dropped across a silicon diode when it conducts?
What is the auxiliary contact called that keeps a contactor pulled in after the START button is released?
A 24 V DC relay coil measures 480 Ω. How many milliamps does it draw?
What is the fault called when current flows from a line conductor into exposed metalwork or the ground?
In a capacitor-start motor, which switch inside the motor cuts out the start winding once the motor is up to speed?
What is a fault called that comes and goes, rather than being there all the time?
An RCD fitted to protect people usually trips at what rated residual current, in milliamps?
What is it called when solder joins two pads on a board that should not be joined?
What do the letters VSD stand for, in motor speed control?
What is the value, in ohms, of a resistor with the colour bands brown, black, red?
Which instrument applies a high DC test voltage, such as 500 V, to check the insulation between conductors and earth?
What is the underlying reason for a fault called, which must be fixed so that the fault does not come back?
In which unit is a resistor's power rating given?

essays.stem: Describe a logical method for diagnosing a fault, from the first report to the handover. Use as your example a borehole pump that keeps stopping.
essays.modelAnswer: First I collect information: I ask the client what happens, when it started, how often, and whether anything was changed or repaired. I read any drawings, the maker's manual and the job history. Next I look and listen. The instructor or a competent person may run the pump so I can see the symptom, for example the overload tripping after twenty minutes. I then think of likely causes, such as a worn pump drawing high current, a wrong overload setting, low voltage or a loose terminal. I safely isolate: switch off, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I test in a logical order, starting with the easiest and most likely causes and splitting the circuit to narrow the search. I record each reading. When I find the fault, I find its root cause, repair it with correct parts, test again dead, and a competent person carries out the function test. Finally I explain to the client what was wrong and write the report.
markingPoints: Gathers information from the client, drawings and history
Confirms the symptom safely and lists likely causes
Isolates safely and tests in a logical order, recording readings
Repairs the root cause with correct parts
Retests, function test by a competent person, report and handover

essays.stem: Explain how you would safely isolate a three-phase motor control panel before testing it for faults, and why each step matters.
essays.modelAnswer: I first find the correct isolator for the panel from the drawings and labels, and tell the people who use the machine that it will be off. I switch off at the isolator, so no current flows. I lock it off with my own padlock and keep the key, so nobody can switch it back on while I work. I fix a tag saying who is working and why, so others know. Then I check my two-pole voltage tester on a proving unit to make sure it works. I test between all phases, each phase and neutral, and each phase and earth at the point of work, because one phase could still be live from another source or a wrong label. I check the tester again on the proving unit, because if it failed during the test, a 'dead' reading means nothing. I also check for other supplies, such as a separate control supply or stored charge in capacitors and drives, and isolate or discharge them. Only then do I start testing.
markingPoints: Identifies the correct isolator and informs users
Switches off, locks off with a personal padlock and keeps the key
Tags the isolator
Proves dead on all conductors with a tester checked before and after, with the reason
Checks for other supplies and stored energy

essays.stem: A breaker on a lighting circuit trips. Explain how you would tell whether the cause is an overload, a short circuit or an earth fault, and how you would find it with dead tests.
essays.modelAnswer: First I ask when it trips. If it trips only after some time with all lights on, an overload is likely: too many fittings for the breaker, or added loads. If it trips at once on reset, there is a short circuit or an earth fault. If an RCD trips rather than the breaker, it points to leakage to earth. Then I isolate the circuit, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I add up the load from the fittings and compare it with the breaker rating to check for overload. For a short or earth fault, I disconnect lamps and drivers, then use an insulation resistance tester between line and neutral, and between line and earth, and neutral and earth. A very low reading shows the fault. I then split the circuit at a junction or fitting and test each part, so each test halves the area. I look closely at the part that fails, repair it, and test again before handing back.
markingPoints: Uses the timing of the trip to separate overload from short circuit or earth fault
Isolates safely, with the tester checked before and after
Checks the load against the breaker rating
Insulation tests between conductors and to earth, with electronics disconnected
Splits the circuit to locate the fault, repairs and retests

essays.stem: Describe how you would test a single-phase capacitor-start motor that hums but will not start. Say what each test result would tell you.
essays.modelAnswer: I isolate the supply, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I discharge the capacitor safely through a suitable resistor, because it can hold a charge. First I turn the shaft by hand: if it is stiff or seized, the bearings or the driven load are the problem. If it turns freely, I test the capacitor with a capacitance meter. If the reading is outside its marked tolerance, or it is open or shorted, it must be replaced with one of the same value and voltage rating. Next I measure the resistance of the run and start windings. The start winding normally reads higher than the run winding; an open reading means a broken winding. I check that the centrifugal switch closes when the motor is at rest, because if it stays open the start winding gets no current. Finally I do an insulation test from the windings to the frame. After the repair, a competent person runs the motor and checks the current.
markingPoints: Isolates safely and discharges the capacitor
Checks that the shaft turns freely
Tests the capacitor against its marked value and tolerance
Tests both windings for continuity and compares them
Checks the centrifugal switch and insulation to frame; function test by a competent person

essays.stem: Explain the precautions you need to take when diagnosing and replacing components on an electronic circuit board.
essays.modelAnswer: The board must be disconnected from its supply, and large capacitors must be discharged, because they can hold charge for a long time. I work on an anti-static mat and wear an earthed wrist strap, and keep new chips in their bags until fitting, so static does not damage them. I take a photo before removing parts, and note the direction of diodes, capacitors and chips, so they go back the right way. I test parts with the board dead, using the diode test, resistance and capacitance ranges, and I remember that other parts on the board can affect a reading, so I may lift one leg. I use a temperature-controlled soldering iron, a solder sucker or braid, and do not overheat pads and tracks. Replacement parts must have the same value, voltage and power rating. I use eye protection and fume extraction while soldering. Afterwards I inspect the joints for bridges and dry joints, clean off flux, and the board is powered and tested by the instructor.
markingPoints: Disconnects supply and discharges capacitors
Uses anti-static protection
Records part positions and orientation
Tests and replaces with correct ratings, avoiding damage to pads and tracks
Soldering safety, inspection of joints and powered test by the instructor

essays.stem: A direct-on-line starter will not start its motor at all. Describe how you would find the fault using the schematic and dead tests.
essays.modelAnswer: I first ask what happened and look for obvious signs such as a tripped overload, a blown control fuse or burnt parts. I read the schematic to understand the control circuit: control fuse, STOP button, START button, overload contact, contactor coil and hold-in contact. I safely isolate the starter, lock off, tag and prove dead with a tester checked before and after. I check the control fuse with a continuity tester. Then I follow the control circuit on the schematic and test continuity of each part in turn: the STOP button should read closed and open when pressed; the START button should read open and close when pressed; the overload contact should be closed when reset. I measure the coil resistance: open circuit means the coil has failed. I also check the main contacts and the motor windings. I write down each result against the schematic. When I find the faulty part, I replace it, retest, and a competent person carries out the function test.
markingPoints: Gathers information and makes visual checks
Uses the schematic to plan the test sequence
Safely isolates with tester checked before and after
Tests each control item (fuse, STOP, START, overload contact, coil) and knows the expected result
Records results, repairs, retests; function test by a competent person

essays.stem: Compare repairing a faulty item with replacing it. Explain what you would consider before advising the client.
essays.modelAnswer: Repairing keeps the existing item and may be cheaper and quicker if the fault is a simple part, such as a capacitor, a contactor or a loose connection. Replacing gives a new item with a warranty, and may be better if the item is old, worn out or no longer safe. Before advising the client I consider the cost of the repair, including parts and labour, compared with the price of a new item. I check whether the parts can be bought in Jamaica and how long they will take to arrive, since a long wait may cost the client more in lost business. I look at the age and condition of the item, how often it has failed before, and whether it still meets safety needs. I think about energy use: a newer motor or light may use less power. If it is under the maker's warranty, the maker may need to deal with it. I give the client the options with prices in J$ and let them decide, and I record the decision.
markingPoints: Explains what repair and replacement each offer
Compares cost of repair with replacement
Considers parts supply and downtime
Considers age, history, safety and energy use
Gives the client options with prices and records the decision

essays.stem: Describe the checks and tests you would carry out after repairing a fault, before the equipment is handed back to the client.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check my own work. All connections are tight, with no bare copper showing and no strands left out. Covers, glands and guards are back in place, and no tools or offcuts are left inside. The replacement parts are the right ratings. Then, with the equipment still isolated, I carry out dead tests: continuity of the protective conductor to all exposed metal, insulation resistance between conductors and to earth, and polarity, so I know it is safe to energise. I compare the results with the expected values and record them. Next, a competent person removes the locks in the right order, energises the equipment and carries out a function test: the motor turns the right way, controls and safety stops work, and the current is normal. I watch it run for a while to make sure the fault does not return. Finally I clean up, explain the repair to the client and complete the job report with the readings.
markingPoints: Visual check of workmanship, covers and ratings
Dead tests: protective conductor continuity, insulation resistance, polarity
Records and compares results with expected values
Energising and function test by a competent person, including safety controls
Observes running, cleans up, reports to the client

essays.stem: Explain why finding the root cause of a fault matters. Use the example of a breaker that keeps tripping on a shop's air-conditioning circuit.
essays.modelAnswer: The root cause is the real reason the fault happens. If only the symptom is treated, the fault comes back, costs the client more and may become dangerous. For a breaker that keeps tripping on an air-conditioning circuit, the easy answer would be to fit a bigger breaker. That is wrong and unsafe, because the cable could then overheat without the breaker tripping. Instead I look for the cause. I check the unit's current against its nameplate, which may show a dirty filter or coil, a failing fan or compressor, or a low supply voltage making it draw more current. I check for loose or burnt terminals at the breaker and isolator, which heat up and can make the breaker trip. I check the breaker is the right type and rating for the unit and the cable. Once the true cause is fixed, for example the coil cleaned by the refrigeration technician and a loose terminal tightened, the breaker stops tripping and the client is protected.
markingPoints: Defines root cause and why treating only the symptom fails
Explains why fitting a larger breaker is unsafe
Lists likely causes: load, dirty coil or filter, failing motor, low voltage, loose terminals
Checks breaker type and rating against cable and unit
Fixes the cause and confirms the fault has gone

essays.stem: Describe what should go in a fault report to a client or supervisor after a repair, and why each part is useful.
essays.modelAnswer: The report starts with the details: client, address, date, the equipment and the person who did the work. It says what the client reported, so the reader knows why the call was made. It lists the tests carried out and the readings, which shows the work was done properly and gives a record to compare with next time. It states the fault found and its root cause, so the client understands what went wrong and how to avoid it. It lists the work done and the parts fitted, with ratings, which supports the bill and any warranty. It gives the results of the tests after the repair, showing the equipment is safe. It notes anything still needing attention, such as worn parts or unsafe wiring nearby, with advice and an estimate, so the client can plan. It ends with the time spent and signatures. A clear, honest report protects the client, the technician and the company.
markingPoints: Job details and the reported problem
Tests and readings taken
Fault, root cause and work done with parts
Tests after repair showing it is safe
Further recommendations and signatures, with the reason each part matters

practical1.title: Find and repair planted faults in a direct-on-line motor starter training panel
practical1.brief: The assessor gives the group a direct-on-line starter training panel (isolator, control fuse, contactor, overload relay, START and STOP buttons and indicator lamps) feeding a small motor, with its schematic. The assessor has planted three or four faults. The assessor energises the panel to show the group each symptom while the group watches from behind the marked line, then switches off. As a group, plan the fault-finding: list the likely causes for each symptom on the fault log. Give each member a fault to lead, with the others acting as tester, recorder and checker. For each fault: isolate, lock off with every member's padlock, tag, and prove dead with a tester checked on a proving unit before and after; discharge and check for stored energy; follow the schematic with dead tests until the fault is found; repair it with the correct part; and retest dead. When all repairs are done and the locks are removed, the assessor energises the panel for a function test. Finish with a fault report for the client.
materials: Direct-on-line starter training panel with motor and schematic, with planted faults (set by the assessor)
Two-pole voltage tester and proving unit
Multimeter and insulation and continuity tester
Group lock-off hasp, a padlock for each member and tags
Spare parts: control fuses, a contactor coil or contactor, auxiliary contact block and wire
Hand tools, ferrules and crimp lugs
Fault log and fault report sheets
photos: The fault log with the likely causes listed for each symptom
The isolator locked off with every member's padlock and a tag
The tester being checked on the proving unit before and after proving dead
A continuity or resistance test on a control part, with the schematic beside it
Each fault found, before the repair
checklist: Listed sensible likely causes for the symptom they led
Isolated, locked off, tagged and proved dead correctly, with the tester checked before and after
Used the schematic to plan a logical test order
Chose the right instrument and range and read it correctly
Found the fault and explained the evidence
Repaired it neatly with a part of the correct rating, and retested dead
Recorded readings and helped write the fault report
Stayed behind the line whenever the assessor energised the panel
safety: Only the assessor energises the panel; the group never works on it while it is live
Every member fits their own padlock before anyone touches the panel
Prove dead with a checked tester before touching any terminal
Keep hands clear of the motor shaft and any moving parts

practical2.title: Diagnose and repair component faults on a low-voltage power supply board
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a 12 V DC regulated power supply training board (bridge rectifier, smoothing capacitor, regulator, fuse and LED indicator), its circuit diagram and a note of the symptoms. The board is fed only from a low-voltage bench supply that the assessor connects. The assessor has planted faults such as an open diode, a failed capacitor, a failed regulator, a blown fuse and a dry joint. As a group, inspect the board by eye and with a magnifier, then test the components with the board disconnected and the capacitor discharged: diode test, resistance and capacitance. Each member finds and replaces at least one faulty part, working on an anti-static mat with a wrist strap, and records the readings before and after on the fault log. When the repairs are done, the assessor connects the supply and the group records the output voltage on load. Finish with a short repair report with a parts list.
materials: 12 V DC power supply training board with planted faults, and its circuit diagram (from the assessor)
Low-voltage bench supply, connected only by the assessor
Multimeter with diode test and capacitance ranges
Temperature-controlled soldering irons, solder, flux, desoldering pump and braid
Replacement diodes, capacitors, regulator and fuses of the correct ratings
